newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania seeks telecoms privatisation adviser.
newsitem.headline: Romania seeks telecoms privatisation adviser.

text.p: Romania will call an international tender in May to designate a consultant for the privatisation programme of state-run monopoly telephone utility Romtelecom RA, a senior official said on Monday.
Communications Minister Florin Pantis said 36 firms would compete in the May 10 tender. He declined to name them.
"Our plan is to privatise, in the initial stage, around 30 percent or Romtelecom," Pantis said. Privatisation, involving the choice of a strategic investor, is expectd to be completed by 1998.
Pantis said his ministry had prepared the draft of a bill turning Romtelecom into a commercial company.

The company could fetch up to $4.0 billion, some estimates say. It employs 55,000 people and has some 2.8 million subscribers. It plans to install 500,000 new land lines for some 400,000 new subscribers this year.
Auditors Coopers and Lybrand have almost completed an evaluation of Romtelecom's 1996 results, to include them in the privatisation offer, ministry sources said.
Last week, Romtelecom trade unions protested against the privatisation programme, fearing job redundancies.
"We will go ahead (with the privatisation) irrespective of pressures of any kind put on us. Of course, we will do our best to keep social costs at a minimum," Pantis said.
Last month, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development agreed to give Romtelecom a $200 million loan to fund its development and privatisation plans.
Under the accord, the EBRD would convert the money in Romtelecom shares when it privatises, at the same price a strategic investor would offer.
In 1992 the EBRD gave Romtelecom a credit of 142 million ECUs to instal a fibre optic telecommunications network.

Romania's privatisation programme, launched in 1995 after long delays, has so far failed to deal with large utilities, including Romtelecom, which form the core of the economy and offer the best hope of attracting big foreign investment.
